reply_text:
The quoted words are on the page, word for word. My reading of admission is **borderline**, because of doubt on parts 2 and 1.

**1. The page.** The page opened. It is Microsoft's own news site (Microsoft Source), dated 2014-02-04, and it prints Nadella's email to employees. That makes it his own words, not a news report. The sentence appears exactly as quoted, under the heading "Why am I here?". The next sentence is also there: the change "will be made possible by … insights from big data, and intelligence from machine learning."

**2. The four parts of the rule**
- **Part 1 (speaker and role): borderline.** He was on his first day as chief executive, so on the role history he held the role. But the reasons the history gives for Microsoft counting are the Phi models, the Microsoft AI models and the Maia chips. As far as I know, all three came about a decade after 2014, and I'm going from memory there, not from the page. In 2014 Microsoft was not plainly a company that builds frontier AI models or chips. The rule doesn't say whether the company has to qualify on the date the words were said. The Tesla ruling suggests that question gets ruled company by company, so it needs your call.
- **Part 2 (forward-looking and about AI): borderline.** The words do look forward. But "computing will become even more ubiquitous and intelligence will become ambient" reads as a broad vision of the computing industry. It doesn't clearly say what AI will do, reach or ship. Machine learning is named only as one of four things behind the change, alongside devices, the cloud and big data. The rule says a truly borderline case stays out and is logged as borderline.
- **Part 3 (date or span): passes.** "Over the next decade" is a span counted from the day it was said, so it would be due at the end of 2024.
- **Part 4 (primary source): passes.** The source is his own words, published by Microsoft.

**3. Already recorded?** No. None of the seven recorded claim files is from 2014 or makes this claim.

One more point if this were admitted: "intelligence will become ambient" sets no test an outsider could check. It would probably be marked `unfalsifiable` at entry.
